what_this_is: The expected output of tools/verdict_v2.py in its four program checks. Part 1 holds the numbers the design spec gives for the old v1.2 labels. Part 2 holds counts worked out by hand for made-up passages, scored from raw label files: the scorer alone, no checker. Part 3 sends the same made-up label files through the checker first (tools/check_labels_v2.py), then scores the rows the checker wrote: the chain the real run uses. Part 4 shows hand-made seals, receipts and label rows to the gate of verdict mode and lists the refusals it must give. Nothing here is a verdict.
how_it_is_used: verdict_v2.py walks every expected block. It prints one line for each value: what is expected here and what the program printed. A key that starts with `_` is a note for a reader and is skipped. E, shares and kappa are text with 3 decimals. A dropped share has 4 decimals. Part 1: `verdict_v2.py old --old-dir verdict --expected <this file>`. Parts 2, 3 and 4: `verdict_v2.py fixture --dir label_v2/fixture`. Seal condition S1 needs all four parts with 0 values that differ.
status_words: Bars, hold table, outcome words and seal conditions are proposals until the owner signs them. In every program check the outcome column reads NOT_A_VERDICT. The key `rule_would_give` shows which word the arithmetic leads to, so that the arithmetic can be checked.

part_2_fixture._note: Five runs on three sets of made-up passages. `spec_six` is the six-passage fixture the design spec writes out (F1 to F6), with the spec's own expected counts. `branches` is 15 more made-up passages (G01 to G15) so that every branch of the scoring is hit at least once. `backstop` is one passage (H01) with 11 broken entries, one for each way the program itself must drop an entry. The two `ruling` runs score the first two sets again under an owner-ruling file. Every count below was worked out by hand before the program ran.
part_2_fixture._note_this_part_is_the_backstop_test: Every set in part 2 is scored from RAW label files. No checker is run. So every drop in this part is made by the scorer's own backstop, and a repeated entry is taken out by the scorer as a duplicate. In the real run the checker comes first: it marks the drops, and it fails a repeated entry (C8), which then stays in its row as a dropped entry. Part 3 tests that chain. Verdict mode and practice mode never score a raw file.
part_2_fixture._note_added_after_the_review_round: Three runs were added after the one review round of the build. `forms` is six passages (J01 to J06). In each one team B writes a form that guide section B2 forbids. `spec_six_bar_row_5_with_twins` scores the six passages with the constant FIVE_BAR_ROW switched to 'with_twins' (sheet item 6). `spec_six_ruling_all_codes_open` scores them under the hold table with every code open. The counts of these three runs were worked out by hand first, and then compared with the program.

outcome_rule_edges._note: No hand-made fixture can reach 50 cases and 50 absences, so every fixture row gives NOT_ENOUGH_CASES. These lines ask the outcome-word rule directly, at each edge of the order the plan gives: 1 too few cases or absences; 2 a bar missed; 3 bars met but more entries outside the bar row than inside; 4 otherwise labelable. The bars used are the proposed ones: E at least 0.80, kappa at least 0.60, 50 cases, 50 absences. If the owner signs other numbers, these lines change with the constants block.

edges._why: One case short of 50. The size rule comes first.
Too few cases and both bars missed: still the size word, because it is first in the order.
Exactly 50 and 50 is enough. E just under 0.80: a failed bar is a failure.
E meets its bar, kappa is just under 0.60: a failure.
Both bars met exactly. As many entries outside the bar row as inside is not 'more outside'.
Both bars met, one more entry outside the bar row than inside: the pass is withheld.
A bar is missed and most entries sit outside the bar row. The withheld-pass rule can only take a pass away. A failure stays a failure.
E cannot be computed. A bar that is not shown to be met is not met.
Kappa cannot be computed. The same.
A clean pass: both bars well met, nothing outside the bar row.

part_3_chain._note: The chain the real run uses: checker first, then scorer. For every set below, verdict_v2.py loads tools/check_labels_v2.py, sends each made-up record through the checker's own three-try loop (take_try), lets the checker write the final rows (final_row), and scores those rows. Three things are compared. `checker_marks`: what the checker wrote, counted from its rows alone. `gate`: the refusal codes the label gate of verdict mode gives for those rows (none are expected). `scorer`: the scorer's output. Where a set names `scorer_as_raw_set`, the scorer must print what part 2 expects for that set, except the values under `scorer_except`. So each difference between the raw run and the chain is written down, with its reason. A broken checker, or a broken hand-over from checker to scorer, shows here as a value that differs. A fixture row with "labeler_failed": true stands for a reply that could not be read: no record is sent on any try. Marks that a made-up label file carries itself (dropped, failed_checks, reasks) are thrown away by the checker, which writes its own.
part_3_chain._how_these_counts_were_made: By hand, from the counts of part 2 and the checker's written rules (guide section B2 and the text at the top of check_labels_v2.py), before the chain was run. Then the chain was run and compared.
